text: Florence, a Rapanui girl. Iorana Korua, I'm Florencia Araki, I live in Easter Island. The island is pretty. The sky is light blue and the clouds are white. My dad works in the Uta on my family's plot. I like to help him. We plant fruits and vegetables. When we make holes a lot of wind to plant the seeds. Then we put agüita. The plants are affirmed in the sticks we put. And they begin to grow and grow. Then we reap Perejíl, tomato, avocado, bananas and many more things. And we have some animals. Chanches, cows and horses. I like to ride the Ilo hole. What I like to do the most is dive, I get snorkel. And we carry an harpoon in case a shark appears. The fish that are most on the island are the pici, the master sword, the Maito and the Titeve. When it scares, it inflates like a balloon and there are many tunas. In hype there is a turtle -shaped pool. Many turtles always arrive, some giants with beautiful caparazones with their children. There are green, blue and coffee. My favorite place on the island is Anakena. Every time an important person died, a moai was made. Raraku Rano volcano took out the stones to make the moais. The moais are very large and heavy. They seem to move them with strings and bananas sticks. They grabbed the Moai and then stopped them in the AHU. There are many ahus throughout the island. The Tapati is a very important party and we do it in February and it comes people from all over the world. What I like most is dance competition. And I danced tamuro with costumes made of feathers or shells called Pitis. We also use crowns made of flowers and other things. And we chose the king and the queen of the island. But in my house the queen is me.

Hello, I'm Isaac and I live in Colchane. Isaac, an Aymara child. Colchane is in the Altiplano in the Andes mountain range. The landscape is very beautiful. There are volcanoes, rivers and geysers. In the summer it rains and in the winter it is so cold that sometimes snow falls. It is very cold. In my house I live with my dad and my brothers. We live so close to the border that sometimes we can go to buy by bicycle. My grandfather Faustino lives in inquelgá. In an Adobe house near the mountain. He is a shepherd and breeds and alpacas. Here are almost all people we have. We lies to us almost everything to live. Meat, leather and wool. We lick them. Floreum is something we do in the New Year, Aymara. We place wool pompoms to the wee we know who they are. When my grandfather is going to walk he takes my Toby dog. I like to accompany him. But you have to get up very early. And it gives me a lot of sleep. That is my Toby dog. It's funny. We lies are very funny. Sometimes the tail is pursued. And jump. And they play as if they were friends. Sometimes we go with my grandfather to his farm to sow. Here we sow Quinoa and Popes. It is almost the only thing that grows. At sunset we have to take the wee to his pen. So that the foxes are not eaten. With my grandfather we also went fishing. Near Calchuri there is a large slope with fed up water. We have a super good technique. We make a pool with stones. And we get caught with a bucket. This is easier to grab them. Here we fish Sutri and trout. LAT LIST YAT or Aguayos are the most traditional fabric. When I was a bus my mother was loaded in a Yi or Aguaya. We also use them to load food. When there is carnival I put my hat that my grandfather of Bolivia brought me. We dressed with very fine costumes. We dance sicuri. And we threw up chaya. The Aimaras believe that Pachamama Our Mother Earth is sacred. We take great care of her. And we appreciate everything that gives us.

Natalia, a Mapuche girl. Mari, Mari, I'm Natalia. Thus we greet the Mapuches. We speak Mapudungun. We live in the community of Mahuidache, a LOF near Temuco. Here it rains a lot in winter. And you can play more because there are trees, there are birds. It is very cute. And there is more patio. My dad helped him to milked the cows every morning. We also take the eggs that put the chickens. You have to do it very early. Here is my cup. My ñaña, my grandmother. My grandmother is Machi. A Machi is a person who cures people. He knows about herbs, heals the sick, directs the ceremonies. And it is very, very important for the community. I really like roasted flour. And it is richer when it is with milk. I love it. Today will be a great day. In ceremonies I look very pretty. Use Tarilonko, silver rings called Shaway, Quilla, which is a warm layer. It is warm. Trapelakucha and Trarihue. Today there is Nguillatún. I like Nguillatún because I share with people. And I also celebrate the We Tripantu which is the new sunrise. Our New Year. We also eat many rich things with the Michenén or Catuto, nicknamed with juice, beans and the muday. I like to take muday and we like to talk a lot. In the Nguilletún we all participate. Tañicucú, my grandmother, touches the kultrun. She directs the ceremony. My dad plays Tructruka and Pifilka. I would like to learn to play the trumpe. Toin, Toin, Toin, Toin, Toin, Toin. It sounds very nice. In this ceremony we ask to have good time. Good harvests. And we thank Newechen for health and life. "

We live on an island in the middle of the Pacific Ocean. Iorana, my friends tell me about and I am a Rapanui child. I live in Hanga Roa, in you whistle or you, also known as Easter Island. My island is full of colors, very green trees, there are many types of flowers and fruits and the earth is red. The island is warm, sometimes it runs a lot of wind. You can walk with a shirt even if it is raining. One of the oldest traditions on the island is the priest. We make a hole on earth, we fill it with stones to hot down. Then a large tray, food, meat, chicken and tuna. On Easter Island, in the sea there are many types of fish. My favorite fish is the manuhe, gray, big and guatón. The Titeve is a balloon fish that inflates when it is scared. But we cannot eat because some are poisonous. The Tapatí is Rapanui's most important party. I danced. My uncle paints my body with Kihea, white, red and black paintings. They paint me Make Make, the God of the Rapanui. And Mantao, the same drawings that carved our ancestors in stone. The Rapanui loves music. When we are all together, my dad plays the guitar. My mom sings. One of my brothers touches the battery. And the other touches the ukelele. I really like singing. One of the things I like the most is to play ball. But what I like most is to row in Vaka Hame. So we tell the canoes here. For the tapatí the races range from Hank Piko to Anakena. One of the most beautiful places on the island is Anakena. Just before arriving at the beach there is a great amú. Amú are sacred places where my ancestors lifted the moais. They remind us of our deceased ancestors. In the Tapatí for the next day they make Hanapico races to Anakena.

Hello, I'm Joel Quinán, a Molulco Huilliche child. Joel, a Huilliche child. Molulco is on the Grande de Chiloé Island. Here it is full of lakes and forests. I live near my school with my dad, my mother, my little brother and my tata Juan. My tata, before bed always tells me Chilotas stories. Some give a lot of scare. Like the caleuche, which is a ghost ship that appears between the fog at dawn. This is my school, the rural artistic of Molulco. It is artistic because we like to sing. In the recess I like to play the dye and frozen with my friends. And there are also many animals. Some savages like the colo cat, the Chilote fox. And the Pudú child, which is like a deer but smaller. We are surrounded by sea. My favorite place is Molulco's estuary. There are many sea stars here. Hello. Sometimes I helped Mariscar my mother. We take clams, choritos and fight. Auch! Ha ha ha. Our richest custom is the curanto. We prepare it outside in a large hole. And we cover it with many hot stones. The priest carries fish, meat, potatoes, seafood, Milcao and Chapalele. We all help a little. And it is very entertaining. We Huilliches on the longest night of the year celebrate the We Tripantu, which is the new sunrise. It is when winter begins. Here is our lonko. Our leader. We all listen to it here with great respect. The lonko tries whenever we help ourselves. A tradition where we live is the Minga. It is when we change the house of a neighbor. Or we help to cut the firewood or harvest potatoes. We all support ourselves. After finishing we get together to share a rich and delicious food. But they do not let me out very late, because according to the legends my grandfather tells me the island of Chiloé is full of strange and dangerous beings.

Maya, Paya, Kimsa, Pusi. Hello, I am learning to tell my language, Aymara. My name is Kristel and I live in the town of Pachica. Kristel, a Aymará girl. Pachica is in a ravine in the middle of the desert. The water of the Tarapacá River is very important for us. We can take and water our crops. Like corn, spinach and parsley onions. My mom is the person I like the most in the world. She works by planting rich vegetables. And when someone needs some to cook, he goes to our farm to buy them. In the farm of my family we have lambs, chickens and guinea pigs, which are mice with a small tail. My favorite animals are the rabbit and the call. I love making them love. We lies are very intelligent. When they go for a walk, they return alone after eating for a while. My favorite game is to catch the Cuyi. We put a box and pursue it all over the pen. Sometimes we do competencies with my friends. I catch you! This is my home. Here I live with my mother, my dad and my three brothers. My mother likes to weave. And weave with a loom. Weaved beautiful belts, warm Anakos and Awuayos of all colors. My mother uses lamb wool, flames or alpaca. The softest of all. We paint the wool with natural dyes, which we take out of the earth and plants. I like when my mother cooks the Kalapurka. This dish is very rich. It has a peeled corn, meat, onion, coriander, garlic, pepper, chili and potatoes. It has many ingredients. I want to learn to prepare it. In winter, every June 21, the Aymaras celebrated our New Year. We climb to the tip of the hill. And we expect the arrival of the first ray of the sun. The Aymaras always thank Mother Earth for all the blessings they give us. Hello, I am Kristel and this is my suit. This is called Aksu. I, my grandmother and my mother we wove it to dance in the Sicuri Carnival.

Hello, I am Camilo and I am seven years old. I live with my dad, I tell him Chinese, because he has very much eyes, so very stretched, very chinitos, so slowly that he uses. My mother smells so rich to flowers, sweets, croissants and in quecs. I tell him pretty. I live with my sister and together we do many experiments. I have two turtles, they are called Maxi and Martina, they are water turtles. I have two dogs, Rafa and Doby. The Rafa is super crazy, steals, toys and to the table are steal. And the Rafa eats a lot of poop. My mom also puts her nervous. Sometimes the boot, my grandmother takes care of every afternoon, we play together and eat apple with salt. I really like going to school. There are many games and friends. I have four companions, Anaís, Martina, Fernanda, Ayleen and I, the only man in the course. And we learn to read in Braile. And my white teacher is the best teacher. With each finger we read books, stories. And my favorite story, Mac the unknown microbe, is very brave like me. Hello. Goalball is a sport that consists of catching the ball and the ball has many sounds. I earned a medal last year in Goalball. I like to ride a bicycle. I have a feeling of jumping to the water and the wind takes me. In my piece there are toys, many instruments, a safe, my secret box only I can open it. In my box there are many secrets. I have many instruments. My favorite is the Güiro, accordion, drums and many more instruments. To make an instrument at home, you need some other jar. Rice, coins, balls, whatever they want is thrown. Then they close it and cover it with the Scotch. And ready, it is already an instrument. I love to go to the fair. There is a lot of noise, there are different textures and different types of smells. Sometimes I help sell. I sell, I sell, I sell the vegetable! What I like most is Friday. Today is Friday and my body knows it. We do entertaining things, we dance and I love the games we do on Friday. One day a strong storm fell and the light was cut. All were scared, except me. I was happier than ever, it was the best Friday of my life. Hello, I am Camilo and I want to inform all children. I want them to be curious because it is incredible.

Hi, I'm Eva and I'm Lickanantai. I live in Toconao, north of Chile, very close to San Pedro de Atacama. Here I live with my mother, my dad and my brother, the Seba. He likes dinosaurs and strange things. It's a little crazy. And I also have a cat called cocoa. My mom put her like this and always bite her feet and break the socks. What I like most to live in Toconao is that there is pure air, it is very quiet and silent. Here is not like the city, we have no traffic lights because there are very few cars. Here in Toconao is the Jere Valley. It is a very nice place. There is a river, pools, orchards, and trees. I like it because my grandparents also went to that place. In the summer we bathe in a pond that is between a forest. We tell you the pool. It is very entertaining. That water also serves to water the orchards. Here the quince, figs and pomegranate plant. The grenade is red and has many pepas and is super sweet. Here in Toconao there are several volcanoes such as Licancabur, San Pedro and San Pablo, El Quimal, The Jurique and Lascar. In Lascar's slope is Old Talabre. There are many precious herbs. With my mom and my grandmother we will collect them. They smell very rich. First we choose them, we cut them with scissors, we clean them, and then take them out hung for several days. There are many and different. We get airampo, which serves for fever. The rich rich is very rich. And the tolilla that was used to help repair broken bones. With her many techitos are made. My mom gives us when we are sick and we always improve. But there are also Yatires, people who heals sick people with ancestral medicines. I also like to help my grandmother dye wool. First, she takes the wool to the sheep, which is ugly and blanquita. He puts them in a bowl, puts the wool and dye. And my grandmother stains them with natural tinctures, such as Betarraga or with Airampo. This gives wool a pink color. It is very pretty. My favorite food is the Patasca. I have cooked with my grandmother. And carries corn, meat, potatoes. She is very rich. We, the Lickanantai, have many traditions, such as payment to Earth. There you thank the Patahoiri, which means Mother Earth. The water, the fruits, everything she gives us is appreciated. You always look at the mountain range and the offerings are delivered. We put a pitcher with Chacha. A very rich smell is burned and comes out. We also make flourishing. A ceremony to put the wool to the sheep. Blue or pink pompoms are placed on the sheep. Thus females are differentiated. That day we dance chururito, a typical song. Chururito, Chururito, as the Lorito is killed. How the churo lorito is killed than a huayrurito. I like to be Lickanantai because you can collect herbs, know many things and follow the traditions of my family. Hello, I'm Eva. Come to Toconao. I will teach you the routes of herbs and traditions and customs. Bye. Pichintún, Pichintún. It goes around. Eagle. What a beautiful pichintún.

title_es: Benjamín un niño de tierra del fuego
text: Hello, my name is Benjamin and I am a Magellan child. That means I live in Tierra del Fuego, in the southern end of Chile. It is called Tierra del Fuego because formerly an original town lived that were called the Onas or Selknam. They made fires that were seen from the ships, so fire was always seen. In Tierra del Fuego it almost always is cold and runs a lot of wind. In winter frost and snow falls. To warm myself I have my poncho and my beret, which heats up my head. And also to walk the pierneras that are hairy and warm. In spring different birds begin to arrive. Loica that is like little and has red chest. The caga that is white, the male and black the female. And the bandurria has a very long peak. We live with my dad, my mom and my sisters Sami in the stay María Eugenia next to the route. And my sister has a cat that likes to walk a lot. It always goes and returns. His name is Temáukel, just like the God of the Selknam. Sometimes we know many tourists from various parts of the world. English, Austrians, Brazilians, Colombians. In Tierra del Fuego the sky looks blue with very white clouds. In the afternoons they look purple pink of all colors like a rainbow. And at night we sometimes see many stars and comets. The other day we were looking at the sky and saw one that exploded as an artificial fire. The wind is very important for us. We have a mill. We use it to generate light. Thus we can have light and load things and watch TV. My dad works in the room. It is the administrator. It takes care of animals, horses, sheep. I really like to help. We give them food, we clean them. And we have many dogs that are guardians of the sheep. They are fox hunters and help us with work. What I like to do the most is surround and walk on horseback. I learned about four years. We go out with my dad and dogs. My school is far from my house, in Cerro Hat. It is called Herro Hat because it is above the hill that looks like a hat. We always do entertaining things with my family. We are going to camp, for a walk and we are close to the Holy Spirit beacon to hunt Sentollas. They are red with shell and have pointed things. They look like giant spiders with many legs. After winter we make the sheep. Then a chopper with a machine that seems to cut hair. They take the wool, then they put them together and take them. The bundles are pressed and sold. Then the sheep are super peladitas. The wool grows again as in a year. I really like to live here for tranquility. Because I can play a lot and I don't have to get up very early. Hello, I'm Benjamin and I live in Tierra del Fuego. I want to tell you that they take care of the environment where they live. Also that they are tolerant and accept the different.

Hello, I am Nahuel, I live on the mountain. I like living here. There are trees, field, there is river. In the summer, I bathe in the river. I threw fourth. Sometimes with my dad we get pyriguines, put a mesh and grab them. And then we bring it with a bottle with water. This is bully, my dog. Play with me, it boots with my feet, I get it like, I make the rod, I do it there. I live with my tata Juan and my grandmother. My tata carrots, onion, potatoes. And we take potatoes. We take them out with pillory. I open the bag and he grabs the handle and throws it away. My grandmother Teresa, weaves a lot with the sticks. HEAJO CALCEta, Pantufla, vest, pants. Very rich kitchen the pantrucas. Pantrucas are mass squares. It has meat, potato, broth. What I like to do the most is walking on horseback. I learned at two years, I like it because it's fun. I have three horses, flower, moon, fonda. The flower is clear brown and white spot. The horses must be taught. Thus they are calm and do not throw people. To horses you have to take care of them a lot. My tata made him a brush, with that we brushed him. You have to give it agüita, bales, sand, oats. That no more. I like to gallop with my tata. We go to Cerro Rosario. There we make a roast. We had a good time. We climb to the hill and we will see the little birds. Here in the mountain we celebrate quasimodo. It's a party. People are on horseback and accompany the curite. Let's see the sick. We dressed as Guaso. Boots, spurs, pants, leggings, shirt and blanket. With a white handkerchief on the head. Mine was bought by my grandmother. It has a cross equal to that of my tata. They go on horseback, go by bicycle and on foot. The horses also dress quasmented. We put a layer. Yellow blue red. We put rattles and bells. It looks very nice. Sometimes we shout like this, live the Christ King! Long live! We shout. The party is very pretty. And many people come. I am Nahuel. I live with my grandfather and my grandmother. I am quasimodist. And when it's bigger I want to be carabinero.

My name is Luisa María, I was born in Bogotá, Colombia and arrived in Chile about three years ago. Colombia is a very beautiful and very big country. In Colombia there are no marked stations as here. There are cities where it is hot and others where it is very cold. In Bogotá, for example, in a single day it dawns, it's cold. Then a lot of heat, then the wind begins and the rain comes. All this in a single day is weird. On the holidays we went to the pool or the beach. The sea there is warm. My mother is called Flor Alba and my dad Manuel and I have a younger sister named Manuela. We play, I tell you stories and spend a lot of time together. Manuela loves running and climbing, she is very naughty. We decided to come to Chile because my mother was offered to work here. I did not agree to the beginning, but then I liked the idea, knowing a new country. I had never left Colombia. The trip was a different experience, an adventure. I was very nervous. I wondered on the plane, will I have friends there? What will my school be like? When we arrived in Santiago, everything caught my attention. The taxi, the food, the city. We thought the city was ordered compared to Bogotá. But the way of talking about Chileans is very different. I still remember when they told me for the first time, Cachay! I did not understand anything. It was fun. We arrived in winter and it was very strong because we were not accustomed. We had never felt so cold. It was terrible and we cold. Now we learned and warm ourselves a lot for the cold time. And I don't like that. But there is one thing that caught my attention from Chile, the earthquakes. In Colombia there are also, but here they are different. And what catches my attention is that Chileans do not get scared. So there one thinks, they know, they have experience. In my course they received me very well. I liked everything because I met my friends. Julieta, Antonia and Renata. We love drawing. We are the artists of the course. Some children only think of the cell phone or tablet. As I have nothing like that, I spend it reading and I show my friends that reading is not a nightmare. From here I like the charquicán, the nickname with the bitch and the choripán. From Colombia I miss a meal that my grandmother made, which is called the paisa tray. But the celebration that I like most in Chile is 18 because they are like all the celebrations they make in Colombia in one. We go to the fondas, we meet many people and have a great time. What I have done most about Colombia is my family. My cousins, my grandparents, I miss everything. When Christmas we spent together. I like Chile a lot, it's a lovely country. If they gave me the option to return, now I would give me some can as they say here. I got used to it, now I am very happy to live in Chile. Hello, I am Luisa María and I am Colombian and now I live in Chile. And I want to tell all the children to change, to change is good, do not be afraid to change.

Hello, I am the Rodrigo. And I Cristóbal. We are brothers. We live on lawn, at the foot of the mountain range. Here there are many hills, trees and there is a river called the Illapel River. We are going to bathe there. Water is super frozen because it comes from the mountain range. It is big and sometimes it is blanquita. Once we played in the snow, we did little angels. And we ate toasted flour with snow. It's pretty here. There are many animals. There are pigs, goats, horses. Here are dogs, chickens, cows. And there is something nice. They are called petroglyphs. They are carved stones that our ancestors made to tell their story. How they were, how they got their food, how they did everything. In my grandmother's house there are many. They are beautiful. We live with my mother, my dad and my brother boy. My dad is a criancero. It has many goats. He goes to the mountain range because the grass is more abundant there. The glove is our puppy that helps my dad go looking for goats. A When he moves from one part he goes with the other dogs. My grandparents live in the house. My grandmother Elsa and my grandfather Pedro. Sometimes we played dominoes. And we go to look for firewood. But the Cristóbal does not like to go because it is lazy. Poh energy runs out. The schools are all far away and we have to get up very early. In Los Perales we go to a multigrade school. We are 12 colleagues. The Emilia, the Ignacia, the Nibaldo, the Rubén and the Richard. José, Simon, Miguel, Marcos and Ricky. Our teacher is called Priscila. She is very nice and always teaches us that we must greet and be educated. We play several things at recess. Taca-Taca and then we go to the rope and then we go to the ball in the long recess. I like Sanchez plays in our selection and won a golden ball. I understood myself. All the people where I live all to the Cordillera de Argentina. A party is called transhumance. We make fires to put cups to take eleven and at night we saw the stars and are usually very beautiful. We take out the milk. What we need for cheese is a mold, we stirred it, we put rennet and salt. We spend the whole summer in the mountain range. We play many things. We play that we are crianance, right? And we sell the cheeses. When I great, I want to be a criancero because almost my whole family was like that. My grandmother is a criancera, my grandfather, there almost all the people are a criancera. After March we return to the house. And the goats also return, but until the next climb to the mountain range. Hello, my name is Rodrigo. And I Cristóbal. We live on the feet of the mountain range. There it is, in a place that is valley, it is very beautiful, there is a river, the oil must be taken care of and not touching them and not taking them.

Hello, my name is Adelaida and they tell me Lala. I live in Punta Arenas, a city that is at the southern end of Chile. There are many sculptures, the sheep, the whale tail and the most important, the Indian's leg. The legend says that if you kiss him, he gives you good luck and returns to Punta Arenas. It is cold here. And my grandmother, I tell her Beli, says that the sun is as an ornament because she almost never heats up. Sometimes there is a lot, a lot of wind. And that's why in the corners there are railings to affirm themselves because the smallest or thinner people can fly. Once my feet got up, I almost flew, it was a lot of fun. I live with my mother, my brother Lucas and my clotary kitten. Almost every day and when the sea is calm like a cup of tea, I can see many dolphins from my window. They jump and play and sometimes very close to the shore. My dad is a sculptor, made the whale tail and also a restorative. He has repaired several monuments such as the sheep is very large and beautiful. My dad does not live with us, but I love to visit him and go for a walk in our twelve wheels. It is entertaining. I also spend a lot of time with my beli. She does several things. Looms, bags, paint. She is a great artisan. And several times we have acted together in a work called Kre'chenen, which means in Selknam "grabbed of the moon". He tells a sad story of how the original peoples were not respected that inhabited these lands and that is why it almost no longer exists. And that's really sad. I love making crafts. I made a house to my clatplay with a cardboard box that has three floors and above is his bed. He has scratched the entire bath curtain. Here in winter a few days snow falls and with my mother I like to go to María Bethy park because there is a lagoon that sometimes freezes. We go with my Trini cousin, but since we don't have ice skates we slide with bags or tires. Here in Punta Arenas every year, in July or August, we celebrated the winteries. Many people gather, more than 3,000 people and after singing the national anthem we run to the sea, which is super ice cream. The murgas and comparsas are also presented, which are groups with very happy and colorful themes. They disguise themselves, make allegorical cars and compete for being chosen the best. This year we participated in the murga fantasies and stories of Magallanes and we were pirates. I had a hat, long boots and a sword. And it was above the ship, which wore thousands and thousands of balloons with the colors of the Magellan flag. I love living here in Punta Arenas. There are many traditions, my city is very beautiful. We live in harmony with beautiful nature and share a lot in family. Hello, my name is Adelaida and I live in Punta Arenas. I want to tell you that I think not everything is garbage. That recycle the bottles they have in the house and that we help recycle to take care of the planet.

Hi, my name is Cristofer, I live in the community of Cauñicu, in Alto Bío Bío. We are Pehuenches. Pehuenche means Araucaria and Che means person. My house is near the mountain range and next to a river called Cawelloco and a volcano called Lavablanca. I live with my dad, my mom, with my grandmother and I tell him Mama Lisa. I have two dogs, the lynch and the Max. Before we had four cats and got into the stove and stole Charqui. And so we had to stay with two, Nahuel and Heidi, which is my gift. When I arrive from school I like playing with my computer and when my nephew comes we played trees and had a great time. I also like to accompany my grandmother who lives next to me. I help you picar firewood, give food to horses and accompany her when she is sad. She tells me that we have to keep the Pehuenche and Chedungun tongue. I know how to speak the Chedungun and tell up to ten. Kiñe, Epu, Kula, Meli, Kechu, Kayu, Reqle, Pura, Aylla, Mari. My grandmother tells me stories like the story of the man who became León. It was a man who fled to a cave and only ate rabbit. Then he realized that he was growing his hair a lot and became a lion. In the winter it falls a lot of snow and is cold and I like to play in the snow. We make snow monkeys and throw ourselves with snow balls. And we also prepare ice cream and mix the snow with juice. Outside my grandmother's house there is a climb and we throw ourselves with nylon down. Once we threw ourselves and go so fast that we collided with a tree. He was entertaining, but I hit my head. My mom put me Llantén, which is a sheet that has a juice to heal the chichones. In spring they come out digueñes, which are a fungus that come out in trees. To get them we throw a stick or make an invention. We eat the digueñes in a salad we put coriander and a lot of lemon. It is super rich. In April we are going to look for pine nuts. The pine nuts are the fruits of the Araucaria. Araucaria is the most sacred tree in our people. Before the pinions were almost the only food ate the Pehuenches. title_es: Lisardo, un niño maya de Yucatán

Sometimes some fall into the water, there I take them out and loose them and you have to rescue them. Honey we eat or make drops to cure eyes, soaps and creams. It is done with a taj that is a thick timber, you put bags or paper, run away in a air time and can take to heaven. Once I did one that almost escapes me. He arrived so up that almost runs on the airplanes. In Tipikal we have many parties like Hanal Pixan which is the day of the dead. We took chocolate and eat pancito and make offerings with what they liked to eat dead. We make a path with orange and yellow flowers, so they know the road and come a little while to visit us. There is also the party of the pa'puúl, there we ask Cháak, god of rain, which rains a lot. We do it in the atrium for San Juan Bautista and we carry singing, with frogs, snakes and iguanos, we break the pitcher and run away and go to the mountain. Here in Tipikal Maní we are Maya and that is very important for us. It is a very special culture. I always think Kaláantej Maayat'aano ', which means "Take care of the Mayan language", this is to learn and speak it to last forever. Hi, I'm Lisardo and I am from Peanut Yucatan, I come to tell all the children that we must take care of bees and adults who stop fumigating with bad chemicals for bees, if not, they die.

And they come together and I give them their meal and your eaglet. But one day one died, he was called Bold and that was very sad. The Mojeños are known for agriculture. We sow corn, rice, cane, banana and cassava. With my dad we go the field and to the chako we go on the horse and I take my chicks in his Asaye, which is a basket made with motorcycle leaves. There in the field we prepare the Earth, we clean it to make it beautiful so that the tiger does not come and eat it to the vaquita. The Mojeños are great fishermen I like to fish. And I am touching the piano and I am learning has touched the flute a little, traversa. We have a very beautiful party called the ichapekene feetta, which means big party. Here comes people sometimes from other countries to see our party. Oh and there is a super fun thing the bound stick, here people get on and fall. We do the Tintirinti procession and there are fed up dances with different costumes. There are the macheteros, the Actu who represent our ancestors, our grandparents; There is the sun, the moon, the star and the tiger. I get out of Moperita, I am with my hat and my guy. I go out with my grandmother and my dad plays the downturn that is made of Paya leaf. And dancing we thank the Holy San Ignacio for taking care of the people. The Mojeños are a very old and valuable culture. I am very lucky to have been born here in San Ignacio and belong to the beautiful Mojeño town full of culture and traditions, it is unique in the world. Here we are in the Isireri lagoon and today I came to give them a message. Take care of Tatá and the Meme, who are the ones who teach us, grandfather and grandmother. Take care of your pets and your animals. Value your family.

title_es: Marlon, un niño yahuas de Perú
text: Hello, my name is Marlon and I live in the Amazon of Peru. Marlon a boy Yaguas from Peru. We are a Native Yaguas community, we live on the shores of the Momón River, here it is surrounded by rivers and trees, and can only be in boat, after an hour of travel. My community is called a new life, we are like 200 people. It almost always is very hot, sometimes it starts running wind and starts to rain the super strong. The Yaguas are great fishermen, my parents and my grandparents taught me. There are three types of fishing: Tarrafear, it is a network where you catch the fish; Anzuelar, is done with a cane and nylon; Flying is done with pure nylon and without cane. In the river you get fish like Cahuara, Bujurqui and Sungaro. Here in the community there are many animals, chickens, dogs, viboras such as Naka Naka and on the mount . In the river there are buffers, they are pink dolphins, they are very large and beautiful, once with my dad, we catch one with the network, but we leave it free. And there are also anacondas, almost always on the shore are very large and super long snakes. They are very dangerous because they catch animals to eat, I am very afraid. Sometimes they change the skin and leave it thrown away, with that skin bracelets, necklace and earrings are made. The river is very special for us Yaguas, because we sail, it gives us food and we also bathe, that is very fun, I go with my brothers and my friends. I am super good swimmer, my mother and dad taught me. I really like to swim and I really like spray. We climb to a large rock, we go to the water, the one that wins the most around. I live with my mom, my dad and my brothers Lislao and Angelo, with them I like to play football. Sometimes we play in the mud, we are very good. With my friends we play football and kiwi, there you put chapitas on the floor, then with the ball you give the chapita, you have to throw them all to win. And I am also going to school and we learn many things. I like to read. But for the Covid I have not been able to go. We listen to classes on the radio. I don't like it that way, because I like playing with my friends there. With my dad we always cut and collect firewood to be able to roast fish, my potato teaches me to hunt and carve the pate. The Pate is like a ball and a mask is split. I do crazy that are like long cerbatanas. Before it was to launch arrows, I do them to sell to tourists. With my mother we make bracelets, necklaces with the chambira, which is a plant that is weaved, we put the seeds of Huasai and Huairuro. We also sell them to tourists in Maloca. The community always comes tourists, we do the Bujurqui dance, when tourists come. The curaca that is the boss, touches the hype. I put my shampa, made with fiber of the water tree. What Yaguas have many legends, one scares me very much but another. The Shapchico is the spirit that protects the animals from the forest, deceiving hunters, makes false footsteps so you can't find it. The Yagua are a special tribe, we live in the jungle very calm, we hunt to feed ourselves, we do not like noise like the city. I like the river and all my community. I like to teach people how our customs are. Hi, my name is Marlon, I live in the Yagua community. We are great fishermen, we take care of what surrounds us. Chao, thanks for seeing us.

title_es: Arony, un niño de Salvador Bahía
text: Arony, a child from Salvador de Bahía, Brazil. Hello! I'm Arony a child from Salvador, Bay. My dad told me that Arony means the guardian of the leaves. Salvador is a very beautiful city. It has many beaches and parks. There are three lanterns, the bar, the Itapuá and that of Humaita, which serves to illuminate the road of the ships. The port of the Salvador arrives super large ships from different parts of the world, Japan, Portugal, Germany and Chile. I live in Cerro Castillo Blanco with my dad Lee and my grandmother Amerinda and my mother Michelle lives in another place, in San Antonio, in the center of the city. I'm always going to see her and we go to the beach together. My house is full of trees because my grandmother loves nature. We have aplanga and cocoa tree, that is my grandmother's favorite. Here in Bahia a long time ago, but very hot, so we always take picolé, which is a super rich ice cream. And they sell it like that! And a bell rifes, there one runs to buy one. There is flavor to corn, kaja and gabiola. The one I like the most is chocolate. With my dad we always go to the stadium to see Bay's games. He is graffiti artist and paints walls about 50 meters. He already painted African things and now he is painting another very large wall. I like to accompany him and see him paint, sometimes I help him a little. I think it's a great job. I have a cagado called Alice and it is dirt, he likes to eat many noni leaves. My grandmother flame her and all the time bites people. It looks like a dinosaur, I love dinosaurs, I'm always drawing them. I like velociraptor, it's fast and hunter. I have a notebook full of dinosaur drawings. When I great I want to be a paleontologist. I really like playing football on the neighborhood court. Sometimes we play without shoes because it is earthly, there I play with my friends Octavio, Lucas and Gabriel. And I like to play goalkeeper and I'm very good. Most in bay are Afro -descendants. The candomblé is the African religion and we go to the Terreiro which is the temple. Orixás are gods and protectors. In the Tororó dike are the statues of the Orixás, they are on the water and are super great. It is oxum, ogum, oxóss, xangô, oxalá, iemanjá, nanã e inesã. I like Oxum, it's beauty and fresh water. Here there are many places that talk about the history of blacks. There is the Church Our Lady of the Rosary of Blacks, there all the saints are black, because before the blacks were slaves and were brought from Africa and were sold as things in the market. And they were mistreated, they were not free and that is very sad and unfair. But there is a very entertaining thing, they are the meetings of Capoeira. The Capoeira is a fight dance, it is fighting but no one is holful. There is music, with Berinbao, Pandeiro, there is sung and fights to the rhythm of music. And we have many parties and ceremonies such as the Bomfim Lavangen Festival that is close to my birthday, there all people dress in white and the bays wash the stairs of the church. And there is the feast of black consciousness that is November 20 and we remember the Zumbi of the Palmares, he was like a superhero for blacks, because he helped his people be free, what is something that all people have to have. I love living here and doing great things with my family and my friends. Hi, I'm Arony, a boy from Salvador Bahía de Castillo Blanco. I hope you like my experience and my video, and my friends and my parents. Bye bye.

Hi, I'm Sofia I live in Tepoztlán, Mexico and I am a Nahual girl. Sofia a Nahual girl, Mexico. Tepoztlán is a very nice place. There are many trees, it's hot and it rains a lot. Above the Tepozteco hill there is a pyramid, the Tepozteco pyramid. My mom tells me that when there is a storm you can see the rays fall but that is very afraid. The place that I like most in Tepoztlán, is the Zocalo, is a place where there are red chairs with a techito, you can go to rest or you can get on the trees, I always go with my mother. I live with my mother Cinthia and my dad Asael, my mother is a nurse, and works at the Women's Hospital, now with Covid she has been working hard. I get sad not to see her so much but I am happy to help others. With my dad we do many things, we play freezbie, we walk by bicycle and as I like football, we always attend the games together. My ball is white, with pink and black, we played with her! I have a cat called Colorín, sometimes he doesn't like to play with me but my dog ​​spark yes! With her we fight for the ball. I also like playing with my dad with him we always play football, but he always wins me because I'm little but one day I will beat him. I go in 2nd Primary, my aunt Monserrat, to which we say mon, is the physical education teacher and sometimes picks me up on her motorcycle and takes me and I love that it takes me !! And when it rains the water from the pudic pudica! What I like most at school is playing with my friends and my premium Mayoli but now it's sad, I can't go to school for pandemic, you can only connect, that is boring. I miss my colleagues. Tepoztlán has a very rich thing. In the town you can eat snow, they are ice cream of many flavors, some have chili or alcohol but there are also strawberry, lemon, pineapple and coconut and I have also tried strange flavors such as rose petal that is like soft but My favorite is the cookie. My great -grandmother Manuela lives very close. I'm always going to see her. She has taught me some words in Nahual as Mistli that means cat and chichito that is puppy. We also do many parties where there are meals and fireworks dances and sweets !! The one I like the most is the Carnival, it is a very fun party where children are going to jump. We put on a chinelo suit and wait for the music band to arrive. Everyone in the town participates in the party, and each one has their suit. Mine made my grandmother. He has some ornaments that I chose, a bunny, a puppy and a butterfly. My grandmother embroidered them, they were very pretty. My suit also has a hat that my grandfather who has some perlitas, which moves when dancing. Another party that I like is the day of the dead. There we disguise ourselves. I once dressed in skull and katrina. My favorite is the vampire. The children go out to ask for sweets, we carry Chilacayotes, mine did it with my dad and in the houses families make offerings for those who have already died. We put candles and things that the dead liked. We put a piglet and bread for my Lupita sister who already died. Here we have many legends about Quetzalcoatl which is the feathered snake of the Nahuas. One day Quetzalcoatl, with a man's body, went out to look for corn because everyone was very hungry, was tired, and hungry. I stop to rest and saw a rabbit. He told the rabbit that I think I'm going to starve and I will not be able to return with corn to save men. Then the rabbit told him, you can't die, eat me, let me hunt and so you can find corn and save men. Quetzalcoatl took it and uploaded it to the moon. I will not kill you, he said, nor will I eat you and put you where you can illuminate everyone with your goodness. I like this legend. I think that legends are special and very entertaining and it is very nice to meet them and it is best to tell them other people and other people and other people.
